sources.title: Groundwater protection position statements
sources.verified_claim: Environment Agency position statements implement groundwater-protection policy using risk-based controls; general policy does not establish a candidate-specific restriction.

sources.title: Groundwater source protection zones: production manual
sources.verified_claim: The Environment Agency defines SPZs using groundwater travel-time and hydrogeological modelling; zone methodology is not an exact candidate intersection result.

sources.title: Protect groundwater and prevent groundwater pollution
sources.verified_claim: The guidance covers permissions, pollution prevention, vulnerability and designated groundwater protection zones for planners, landowners and permit applicants.

sources.title: Protect groundwater and prevent groundwater pollution - full guidance
sources.verified_claim: Activities that may discharge pollutants to groundwater can require a permit and abstractions above relevant thresholds can require licensing; exact activity and location facts are essential.

sources.title: Groundwater protection
sources.verified_claim: The official collection separates permits, technical guidance, position statements and contamination risk assessment; these are distinct evidence families rather than parcel findings.

sources.title: Groundwater source protection zones (SPZs)
sources.verified_claim: SPZ1, SPZ2 and SPZ3 identify increasing travel-time/catchment relationships around potable abstractions and are used to screen development and pollution risk; exact site location must be checked.

sources.title: Source Protection Zones [Merged]
sources.verified_claim: The current public dataset provides merged SPZ outlines as an initial screening layer; exact polygon intersection and current dataset version are required for candidate use.

sources.title: Drinking Water Safeguard Zones (Groundwater)
sources.verified_claim: Groundwater Safeguard Zones target additional pollution-control measures around drinking-water sources and may differ from SPZ boundaries; they require separate spatial matching.
